These examples show live tracking on a map with arrival time, a progress bar, the pro with call and message buttons, the vehicle, a door code and a status timeline, then the finished job with photos, parts, a receipt against the estimate, a tip and a rating.
tips: Lead with the arrival time in large type and keep it inside the booked window.
Show who is coming and how to recognise them (photo or initials, vehicle, plate).
A door or safety code lets the customer confirm the right person arrived.
On the receipt, compare the final total with the estimate and itemise approved parts.
faq: What should a live tracking screen show?
Arrival time, minutes away, a map with route, who is coming with contact buttons, and a short status timeline.
When should I ask for a rating and tip?
On the job-done screen, together with the receipt and payment, while the visit is fresh.

account-email.h1: Transactional email templates (welcome, verify email, magic link, password reset, invoice)
account-email.intro: Account emails are the ones people actually open: they’re waiting for them. These templates cover a welcome email with a getting-started checklist, email verification with a code, a magic-link sign-in, a password reset and a paid invoice. Each is table-based HTML with inline styles, a 600px layout that goes fluid on phones, a bulletproof button and dark-mode colours, in eight visual styles.
tips: Put the one action in a big button near the top, and repeat it as a plain link for clients that block buttons.
Say how long a link or code is valid (15 minutes, 60 minutes, 24 hours) so people know whether to hurry.
For sign-in and reset emails, show when and from which device the request came, and what to do if it wasn’t them.
Use hidden preheader text: it’s the line that shows after the subject in the inbox.
faq: Why are email templates built with tables?

Several widely used email clients, Outlook for Windows in particular, ignore modern CSS layout such as flexbox and grid. Nested tables with role="presentation" and inline styles are the most reliable way to keep the layout intact everywhere.
Do these emails support dark mode?

Yes. Light colours are inline, and a prefers-color-scheme block (plus Outlook.com’s data-ogsc selectors) swaps in the dark tokens from the DESIGN.md. Some clients still invert colours on their own, so test in the clients your users have.
Can I use these with my email provider?
Yes. They’re plain HTML, so they work with any sending service or framework. Replace the example links and copy with your own merge fields.

order-email.h1: Order receipt and shipping update email templates
order-email.intro: After checkout, the order emails are where a store earns trust. These templates show an order receipt with product rows, totals, the shipping address and payment method, and a shipping update with a five-stage delivery tracker, arrival date and tracking number. Table-based, inline-styled HTML for email clients, in eight styles with light and dark colours.
tips: Lead with the order number and the delivery estimate: they’re what customers look for first.
List each item with a thumbnail, variant and price so the receipt can be checked at a glance.
On shipping updates, show progress as named stages, not just a percentage.
Say what happens if nobody’s home, before they have to ask.
faq: What should an order confirmation email include?

The order number and date, each item with quantity and price, subtotal, shipping, tax and total, the shipping address, the payment method (last four digits only), a delivery estimate and a link to view or change the order.
How do you show delivery progress in an email?
A row of table cells works everywhere: one cell per stage with a filled bar for stages already reached and a muted bar for the rest, with the current stage label in bold.

shift-scheduler.intro: A shift scheduler has to show who works when, at a glance, and flag problems before the rota goes out. These examples show a week grid of team members against days, colour-coded shifts by role, open shifts that need cover, time off and unavailability, scheduled against contracted hours, a short-staffed warning and daily labour totals, with a mobile day view.
tips: Keep one row per person and one column per day; put open shifts in their own row at the top.
Colour shifts by role, and always pair the colour with a text label.
Show scheduled vs contracted hours next to each name and flag overtime.
Warn on days below minimum staffing before the manager publishes.
faq: What does a shift scheduling screen need?
A week (or day) grid, shifts with start and end times and role, open shifts, time off and availability, hours per person, daily totals, and a draft-then-publish step so staff only see the final rota.
How should time off appear on a rota?
As a hatched or muted block in the person’s row, labelled with the type (annual leave, unavailable), so it can’t be mistaken for a shift.

leave-calendar.intro: A leave calendar answers two questions: when is this person off, and who else is off then? These examples show one team member’s month with annual leave, a sick day and a half day, teammates who are also away, leave balances with progress bars and upcoming requests, on web and mobile.
tips: Mark leave types with colour and a written label, and add a legend.
Show balances next to the calendar so people see the effect of a request.
Flag teammates who are off on the same days to make clashes obvious.
Let the view switch between one person and the whole team.
faq: What should a time-off calendar show?
Approved and pending leave by type, today’s date, weekends, other people off on the same days, and the remaining balance for each leave type.

time-off-request.h1: Time-off request and approval UI examples
time-off-request.intro: Time-off requests go both ways: an employee asks, a manager decides. These examples show a request form with leave type, dates, half-day options, a note and the shifts it releases; the same form when a day would drop below minimum staffing; and a manager’s review with a coverage check and approve or decline buttons.
tips: Show the balance before and after the request in the form, not after submitting.
Check staffing as the dates are picked and suggest a colleague who can cover.
Give the manager a per-day coverage table, not just the dates.
Make approve and decline equally easy to find, with an optional reply.
faq: How should a leave request handle staffing conflicts?
Explain which day and shift would be short, mark the date fields, and offer a way forward, such as asking a named colleague to cover or moving the dates, rather than just blocking the request.
What does a manager need to approve time off?
Who is asking, the type and dates, the balance afterwards, the shifts affected, whether each one is covered, and any overlapping requests.

ops-dashboard.intro: An owner running several shops needs today in one view. These examples show sales, orders, average ticket, labour cost and staff on shift for all locations, a card per location with sales against target, sales per hour by location and a needs-attention list for low stock, late clock-ins, late deliveries and offline equipment.
tips: Lead with today’s totals, then break them down by location.
Compare each location with its own target, not with the others.
Put alerts that need a person in a short list, each with one action.
Give each location a consistent colour across cards and charts.
faq: What KPIs belong on a retail or café operations dashboard?
Sales so far today against target, orders, average ticket, labour cost as a share of sales and staff on shift, broken down by location, plus live alerts.

inventory-stock.h1: Inventory and low-stock UI examples (with receive stock form)
inventory-stock.intro: Inventory screens are about what to reorder and what just arrived. These examples show a low-stock table with on hand against par level, stock bars, Low, Critical, Out and On order badges, suggested order quantities and bulk purchase orders, plus a receive-delivery form with ordered against received quantities and a shortage note.
tips: Sort by urgency and show on hand against par level, not on hand alone.
Use badges with words (Low, Out, On order), not colour alone.
When receiving stock, start every line at the ordered quantity and highlight differences.
Update counts only when the person confirms, and say so.
faq: What is a par level?
The quantity a location wants on hand after each delivery. Items below it are flagged as low, and the difference suggests how much to reorder.

savings-goal.h1: Savings goal UI examples with projection chart
savings-goal.intro: A savings goal screen should show progress and when the goal will be reached. These examples show a progress ring, amount saved against the target, the month the goal is on track for, a balance chart with a dashed projection to the goal line and a faster what-if scenario, an auto-save slider and round-up toggles.
tips: State the expected finish date in words, next to the progress.
Draw the projection as a dashed line so it can’t be mistaken for real history.
Let people try a different monthly amount and see the new date straight away.
Show other goals with simple bars to keep the focus on one.
faq: How do you show a savings projection?
Plot the saved balance as a solid line and continue it as a dashed line at the planned monthly amount until it meets a goal line, then label the month it gets there.

onboarding-carousel.intro: An onboarding carousel gets a few seconds to explain an app. These examples show the first of three slides for a skincare app: a drawn illustration, a large display headline, a short paragraph, page dots, Skip and a Continue button, with benefit rows on the wider web layout.
tips: One idea per slide, with a headline people can read in two seconds.
Keep Skip visible on every slide.
Show progress with dots and name the step for screen readers.
Make Continue the only filled button.
faq: How many onboarding slides should an app have?
Usually three or fewer. Each should explain one benefit; anything else is better taught in context later.

scored-comparison.intro: A scored comparison goes further than checkmarks: it rates each option on weighted criteria and says how the scores were measured. These examples compare three placeholder plans with overall score rings, six weighted criteria with 0–10 bars, footnote markers and a numbered sources list, on web and mobile.
tips: Publish the weighting next to the table so readers can judge the overall score.
Highlight the best score in each row, not just the winner overall.
Number the footnotes and keep methods short, dated and specific.
Don’t let the recommended column hide that another option scores higher.
faq: How do you calculate a weighted score?
Multiply each criterion’s score by its weight, add the results and divide by the total weight. With weights in percent adding to 100, that’s the sum of score × weight ÷ 100.
Why add sources to a comparison table?
Footnotes show how each score was measured and when, so readers can check it and you can update it when things change.

restaurant-website.intro: A casual dining restaurant home page has one job: get people to book, order or walk in. These templates put hours and a booking path in the first screen, then the menu as text with prices and dietary codes explained by a sample key, ways to eat, group bookings, the kitchen team, questions and a map or contact form.
tips: Show hours, address and a booking button before anything else; most visitors arrive asking “are you open, and can I get a table?”
Put the menu on the page as text, not a PDF, so it reads well on phones and can be found by search.
Mark dietary codes next to each dish, explain them in one key, and check every allergen with the kitchen before you publish.
Offer walk-in and group options so the page answers more than one kind of visit.
faq: What should a restaurant website include?
Opening hours, address and directions, the menu as text with prices, a way to book or order, private dining or events if you offer them, and contact details.
Should a restaurant menu be a PDF?
An HTML menu is easier to read on a phone, loads faster and can be updated without redesigning a file. Keep a printable version as an extra if you need one.

agency-website.intro: An agency site sells with its work. These templates lead with a positioning line and a project brief button, then selected work with client and discipline, services, process, the studio, results and an enquiry form with budget and timeline.
tips: Show three to six projects you’d happily do again, not everything you’ve ever made.
Name the services in the words clients use when they search.
Explain the process in a few steps so a first-time buyer knows what happens next.
Ask for budget range and timeline in the enquiry form to qualify leads early.
faq: What makes a good agency website?
Clear positioning, strong selected work with context (client, problem, result), plainly named services, a visible process and an easy way to start a project.
How many projects should an agency website show?
Usually three to six case studies on the home page, each linking to a fuller write-up.

architecture-website.intro: Architecture websites are judged on restraint and imagery. These templates pair a quiet type-led hero with a filterable project portfolio, the practice’s approach, service stages from feasibility to handover, the studio and an enquiry form.
tips: Let large project images carry the page and keep text short and specific.
Filter projects by sector so clients find work like theirs.
Spell out the stages you cover so clients know where you start and stop.
Give each project its location, year and scope.
faq: What should an architecture firm website include?
A curated project portfolio with location, year and scope, the practice’s approach, services by stage, the team and a simple way to enquire.
How should architects show projects online?
Large images with a short description, the brief and key facts, grouped by type (residential, cultural, workplace) so visitors can browse what’s relevant.

wedding-website.intro: A wedding website answers guests’ questions before they ask. These templates include the date and a countdown, your story, the day’s schedule, venue and travel details, the wedding party, registry, an FAQ and an RSVP form with meal choices.
tips: Put the date, place and RSVP deadline at the very top.
Give one schedule with times and addresses, and say what to wear.
Answer the awkward questions (kids, plus-ones, parking) in the FAQ.
Keep the RSVP short: attending, names, meal choice and dietary needs.
faq: What should a wedding website include?
The date and venue, a schedule, travel and accommodation, dress code, registry, an FAQ and an RSVP form.
When should you send out a wedding website?
Usually with the save-the-dates, then update it with the schedule and RSVP details before invitations go out.

ecommerce-website.intro: A store home page should move people from browsing to a product fast. These templates include an announcement bar, search and cart, a campaign hero, shop-by-category tiles, a best-sellers grid with ratings and swatches, a promo band, shipping and returns facts, reviews and a newsletter.
tips: Make search and the cart visible on every screen size.
Lead with categories and best-sellers so first-time visitors can browse without a plan.
State shipping, returns and delivery times plainly near the top.
Keep product cards consistent: image, name, price, rating and one action.
faq: What should an ecommerce home page include?
Search, cart, a clear hero or campaign, category navigation, best-selling products, shipping and returns information, reviews and a newsletter sign-up.
Can I use these templates with a store platform?
Yes. They are plain HTML and CSS with a DESIGN.md of tokens, so you can port the layout and styles into your store theme or a framework.

coffee-shop-website.h1: Cafe and coffee shop website templates
coffee-shop-website.intro: A café site needs to answer “what’s good, where are you, are you open?” These templates show today’s bakes, a coffee menu with prices, each location with hours, catering and wholesale, the story and an order-ahead form.
tips: Show each location with its own hours and address.
List the menu as text with prices, and mark what sells out early.
Give regulars a fast path: order ahead or pick-up times.
Use warm, specific copy about what you bake and brew.
faq: What should a coffee shop website include?
The menu with prices, locations and opening hours, ordering or pick-up options, catering or wholesale information and a short story.
Do small cafés need a website?
A simple one-page site helps people find your hours, menu and address in search and maps, and gives you a place for catering enquiries.

salon-website.intro: Salon clients want to see prices, durations and who will do their hair. These templates include a booking hero, a price list by category with durations, stylists by level, looks, first-visit and consultation info, a booking widget with time slots and reviews.
tips: Publish prices and how long each service takes.
Show stylists with their level and specialities so clients can choose.
Let people book in a few steps: service, stylist, day, time.
Explain consultations, patch tests and the cancellation policy up front.
faq: What should a salon website include?
Services with prices and durations, the team, a gallery of work, online booking, location and hours, and policies such as cancellations.
How do salon websites get more bookings?
Make booking available from every section, keep the price list easy to scan on a phone and show real availability.

real-estate-website.intro: A real estate agency site starts with search. These templates include a buy and rent property search, listing cards with price, beds, baths and status, a map of the areas covered, a valuation request for sellers, landlord services, fees in plain words and the agents.
tips: Put the property search in the first screen, with buy and rent tabs.
Show the facts on every listing card: price, beds, baths, size and status.
Give sellers their own path, such as a free valuation request.
Add neighbourhood guides to help buyers who don’t know the area.
faq: What should a real estate website include?
Property search, listings with key facts and photos, neighbourhood information, agent profiles, a valuation or contact form for sellers and recent market figures.
How do real estate websites generate leads?
With property alerts, valuation requests and viewing bookings placed next to the listings people are already browsing.

construction-website.intro: Builders win work on trust and clarity. These templates include a quote-request hero, services, recent projects with scope and duration, a process timeline, licensing and insurance facts, figures and a quote form with project type, budget range and start date.
tips: Show finished projects with scope, duration and location.
Explain your process from first visit to handover.
State licences, insurance and warranties plainly.
Ask the right questions in the quote form so you can price the job.
faq: What should a construction company website include?
Services, a project portfolio, the process, licensing and insurance details, testimonials and a quote request form.
How do I get more quote requests from my website?
Put the quote button in the header, keep the form short but specific (project type, budget, start date, postcode) and show recent local work.

law-firm-website.intro: A law firm site has to feel clear and approachable. These templates include a consultation hero, practice areas, how fees work, attorney profiles, articles, client notes, a consultation request form and a disclaimer line in the footer.
tips: Name practice areas in plain words, not just legal terms.
Explain how fees work (fixed fee, hourly, first consultation).
Show the people clients will actually work with.
Keep the contact form short and say how quickly you reply.
faq: What should a law firm website include?
Practice areas, attorney profiles, how fees and consultations work, articles or guides, contact details and any disclaimer your jurisdiction requires.
Do law firm websites need a disclaimer?
Many jurisdictions expect one, for example that the site is not legal advice and contacting the firm does not create a client relationship. Check your local rules.

dental-website.intro: Patients choose a dentist on convenience and comfort. These templates include a booking hero with the next available time, services, new-patient steps, insurance and payment information, the dentists, the practice, hours and location and a booking form.
tips: Show the next available appointment and a phone number up top.
List services plainly, including emergency visits.
Explain what happens at a first visit.
Be specific about payment options and insurance without promising outcomes.
faq: What should a dental practice website include?
Services, online booking, new-patient information, insurance and payment options, the team, opening hours and location.
How can a dental website help nervous patients?
Calm design, real photos of the team and rooms, and a clear description of a first visit help people know what to expect.

gym-website.intro: A gym site should make the first visit easy. These templates include a free-trial hero, a weekly class timetable, membership options, coaches, the training floor, a beginner path, member notes and a trial booking form.
tips: Put the timetable on the page, not behind a download.
Show membership options side by side.
Give beginners their own path and say what a first session looks like.
Introduce coaches with their focus areas.
faq: What should a gym website include?
Class timetable, membership options, coaches, the facilities, a beginner or trial offer, location and opening hours.
How do gyms convert website visitors?
A free or low-commitment trial class, a clear timetable and honest information about what to expect on the first visit.

school-website.intro: A school website serves prospective families first. These templates include a visit-and-apply hero, the stages of the school, an admissions timeline with key dates, academics and co-curricular life, campus life, news and events and an open-day registration form.
tips: Put open days and the admissions timeline where families can’t miss them.
Explain each stage of the school simply.
Show daily life: clubs, sport, arts, lunch and transport.
Keep news current; stale news signals a stale school.
faq: What should a school website include?
Admissions information and key dates, the curriculum by stage, co-curricular activities, news and events, contact details and a way to book a visit.
How do school websites support admissions?
With clear timelines, open-day booking, fees or financial-aid information where relevant, and real stories of school life.

nonprofit-website.intro: A nonprofit site turns interest into support. These templates include donate and volunteer calls to action, impact figures, programmes, how donations are used, volunteer shifts, events, stories and a donation form with amount options and monthly giving.
tips: Give two clear actions: donate and volunteer.
Show what a donation pays for in concrete terms.
Report your own figures and say where they come from.
Make monthly giving an easy option in the form.
faq: What should a nonprofit website include?
Your mission, programmes, impact, ways to give and volunteer, events, stories and registration or transparency information.
How can a nonprofit website get more donations?
Make the donate button visible everywhere, show what each amount does, keep the form short and offer monthly giving.

travel-website.intro: Travel sites sell a feeling and answer logistics. These templates include a trip search, featured trips with days, group size, price and difficulty, destinations, how a trip works, responsible-travel notes, traveller notes and an enquiry form.
tips: Show trip length, group size, price and difficulty on every card.
Explain what’s included and what isn’t.
Use big scenery, but keep the facts readable on top of it.
Offer a brochure or enquiry option for people not ready to book.
faq: What should a tour operator website include?
Trip search, trip pages with itinerary, dates and price, what’s included, how booking works, traveller reviews and contact options.
How do travel websites build trust?
Clear prices and inclusions, small-group details, named local guides, honest reviews and easy contact before booking.

hotel-website.intro: A hotel home page should make availability the easiest thing to check. These templates include a booking bar, rooms and suites with rates, dining, spa and amenities, the neighbourhood, offers, guest notes and location.
tips: Keep the date and guest booking bar visible near the top.
Show each room type with its size, view and from-rate.
Sell the place, not just the room: dining, spa and the area.
Make the address, parking and arrival details easy to find.
faq: What should a hotel website include?
A booking bar, room types with photos and rates, amenities, dining, offers, location and directions and contact details.
How can a hotel website get more direct bookings?
Make checking availability fast, show the best rate clearly and add direct-booking perks such as flexible cancellation.

saas-landing-page.intro: A SaaS landing page explains the product in seconds and earns a sign-up. These templates show a hero with real product UI, team-size proof, features, how it works, integrations, pricing tiers, an FAQ and a closing call to action.
tips: Show the product in the hero, not an abstract illustration.
Lead with the problem you solve in the customer’s words.
Keep plans to three and explain who each is for.
Answer objections (setup time, data, cancellation) in the FAQ.
faq: What should a SaaS landing page include?
A clear headline, product screenshots, key features, how it works, integrations, pricing, social proof, an FAQ and a sign-up call to action.
How long should a SaaS landing page be?
Long enough to answer the main questions a buyer has before signing up, usually seven to ten sections, with the call to action repeated.

ai-website.intro: AI product sites need to show what the tool actually does. These templates include a hero with a prompt-box demo, use cases, how answers cite sources, data-handling facts, workflow steps, pricing, an FAQ and a waitlist or sign-up call to action.
tips: Show a real example prompt and answer in the hero.
Explain how the product handles sources and data in plain words.
Group use cases by job, not by feature.
Avoid vague claims; specific examples persuade more.
faq: What should an AI startup website include?
A concrete demo, use cases, how it works, data and privacy information, pricing, an FAQ and a sign-up or waitlist.
How do you build trust on an AI product website?
Show real outputs with sources, explain data handling plainly and avoid promises the product can’t keep.

medical-website.intro: Patients come to a medical website to get something done. These templates open with a task panel for booking, prescriptions and results, then cover a clinician directory, new patient registration, a portal sign-in, opening hours, after-hours routing and general health topics.
tips: Put the common tasks first: book, repeat prescription, test results.
Say where to go when the practice is closed.
Let people filter clinicians by what they need.
Keep health articles general and have a clinician review them.
faq: What should a medical practice website include?
Ways to book, request prescriptions and see results, clinician profiles, registration steps for new patients, opening hours, after-hours routing, payment information and accessibility details.
Can I use sample medical copy on a real site?
Use it as a starting point only. Replace the sample practice, people and text with your own, and have a qualified clinician review anything health related before it goes live.

cardiology-website.intro: A cardiology site serves two audiences: patients and the clinicians who refer them. These templates include separate paths for each, a referral pathway, a tests and procedures table, a list of what the practice sees, cardiologist profiles and a booking form.
tips: Give referring clinicians their own clear route and phone line.
Explain each test in plain words: what it is, how long it takes, how to prepare.
Show emergency guidance near the top of the page.
List your real registrations and accreditation yourself, never sample ones.
faq: What should a cardiology website include?
Conditions seen, tests and procedures, a referral route for clinicians, how to prepare for a first appointment, cardiologist profiles, locations and emergency guidance.
Why does a cardiology site need a referral section?
Many patients arrive through another clinician, so a clear referral route with the details you need and a direct contact saves time for both practices.

dermatology-website.intro: Dermatology clinics often run medical and cosmetic services side by side. These templates keep both clear, with a skin check journey, a secure photo enquiry, a conditions grid, cosmetic treatments with guide prices, clinician bios and a booking form.
tips: Separate medical care from cosmetic treatments so people find the right one.
Explain what a skin check involves and how results are shared.
Say how photos are stored if you accept them online.
Check your local rules on advertising cosmetic treatments.
faq: What should a dermatology website include?
Conditions treated, medical and cosmetic services, what a skin check involves, prices for self-pay treatments, clinician profiles and how to book.
Can a dermatology website show before and after photos?
It depends on where you practise. Many places restrict them, so check your local rules. These templates do not use them.

therapist-website.intro: Someone reading a therapist's website is deciding whether to reach out. These quiet, text-led templates cover who the practice is for, the first session, fees and sliding-scale places, confidentiality, an FAQ, a crisis note and a very short enquiry form.
tips: Write in the first person and keep it plain.
Publish your fees and cancellation policy.
Say who you may not be the right fit for, and where they can go instead.
Include a crisis note and make the enquiry form short.
faq: What should a therapist website include?
Who you work with, how you work, fees and session length, what the first session is like, confidentiality, a crisis note and an easy way to get in touch.
Should a therapist publish fees online?
Many do, because it saves people an awkward first call. If you offer reduced-fee places, say so plainly.

physical-therapy-website.intro: People look up a physical therapist because something hurts. These templates start there, with a body map that links to conditions by area, then cover a first course of care, programmes, a class timetable, prices, clinicians and a booking form.
tips: Let people start from where it hurts.
Explain what a first session looks like and what to wear.
Say whether a referral is needed where you practise.
Show session length and self-pay prices.
faq: What should a physical therapy website include?
Conditions by body area, what happens in a first session, programmes, session length and prices, clinician profiles, location and online booking.
Do physical therapy patients need a referral?
It varies by country, region and insurance plan, so state the rule that applies to your clinic.

veterinary-website.intro: Pet owners want to know you see their animal and what to do when it can't wait. These templates include a patient picker by species, a wellness plan table, a new pet checklist, out-of-hours routing, the vet and nurse team and a booking form with pet details.
tips: Show which animals you see, including small pets.
Put out-of-hours routing where it is easy to find.
Lay out wellness plans in a simple table.
Ask for pet name, species and age in the booking form.
faq: What should a veterinary website include?
Species seen, services, urgent and out-of-hours routing, wellness plans, the vet and nurse team, prescription requests, opening hours and booking.
How do you present pet wellness plans?
A short table by life stage with the monthly price and what each plan includes works well, so owners can compare at a glance.

financial-advisor-website.intro: Choosing a financial advisor comes down to fit and clear fees. These templates are built around booking an intro call, with planning by life stage, a plain fee table, what the first 90 days look like, a sample plan, how conflicts are handled and an FAQ.
tips: Publish how you are paid in plain words.
Speak to life stages, not products.
Show what the client actually receives.
Have compliance review the page and never imply returns.
faq: What should a financial advisor website include?
Who you work with, how you are paid, your planning process, what clients receive, adviser profiles, any required disclosures and an easy way to book a call.
What disclosures does a financial advisor website need?
It depends on your regulator and country. Check the wording with your compliance contact before publishing.

cleaning-service-website.intro: Cleaning customers want a price and a date. These templates lead with an instant quote card, then show a room-by-room checklist for standard, deep and move-out cleans, recurring plans, what happens on the day, areas served, reviews and booking.
tips: Put a quote form in the hero.
Spell out what each type of clean includes.
Say how keys and access work.
List the areas you serve so local visitors know you cover them.
faq: What should a cleaning service website include?
A quick quote, what's included in each clean, recurring plan prices, areas served, how access works, reviews and booking.
How do you price cleaning on a website?
Most sites estimate from home size, bathrooms, frequency and extras, then confirm the final price after the first visit.

hvac-website.intro: When the heat is out, people want someone on the way. These templates include a 24/7 emergency bar, a symptom picker, today's arrival windows, a service area check, repair, install and replacement options, a maintenance plan table and booking.
tips: Keep the phone number and emergency bar at the top.
Let people start from the problem, not the service name.
Show arrival windows and your service area.
Lay out maintenance plans in a simple table.
faq: What should an HVAC website include?
A visible phone number, emergency service details, repair and installation services, service area, maintenance plans, financing, reviews and booking.
How do you lay out HVAC services?
Start from what the customer is noticing, such as no heat or a strange noise, then route to repair, tune-up or replacement.

cybersecurity-website.intro: Security buyers want to see the product and how it runs. These templates open with a coded findings console, then cover what gets scanned, a triage workflow, audit evidence, how deployment works, security of the product itself, pricing and a demo request.
tips: Show the product early, with realistic findings.
Use real engineering language, not fear.
Explain deployment and permissions plainly.
Only claim certifications you actually hold.
faq: What should a cybersecurity website include?
What the product covers, sample findings, how it deploys, integrations, how you secure your own product, pricing and a way to request a demo.
How do you build trust on a security website?
Show how the product works, explain the access it needs and publish your own security practices. Specifics do more than scary statistics.

crm-landing-page.intro: A CRM page has one job: show a team what their pipeline would look like. These templates include a coded pipeline board, a spreadsheet import mock, follow-up reminders, a forecast view, a rule builder, per-seat pricing, a comparison and an FAQ.
tips: Show the pipeline in the first screen.
Make switching from spreadsheets look easy.
Keep per-seat pricing simple.
End with one clear call to action.
faq: What should a CRM landing page include?
A view of the product, the problem it replaces, key features, import or migration help, pricing, customer proof, an FAQ and one main call to action.
How do you show a CRM on a landing page?
A real-looking pipeline board in the hero works well, because visitors see their own work in it straight away.

coaching-website.intro: People hire a coach they trust, so these personal-brand templates lead with the person. They include a comparison of coaching, mentoring, therapy and consulting, an engagement map with packages, a sample session, a discovery call calendar, essays and an FAQ.
tips: Say clearly who you coach and who you don't.
Explain how coaching differs from therapy and consulting.
Show packages and prices.
Offer a free discovery call and make no income promises.
faq: What should a coaching website include?
Who you work with, your method, packages and prices, what a session is like, client notes, and a way to book a discovery call.
Should coaches publish prices?
Many do because it filters enquiries and builds trust. If yours vary, publish a starting price.

pest-control-website.intro: People search for pest control when they have just seen something. These templates start with a pest identifier, then cover what a visit involves, one-off and quarterly plans, safety for children and pets, service areas, reviews and booking.
tips: Let people start from the pest they saw.
Explain what happens on a visit.
Show one-off and recurring plans side by side.
Be specific about preparation and safety for pets and children.
faq: What should a pest control website include?
Pests treated, what a visit involves, one-off and recurring plans, safety guidance, service areas, reviews and booking.
How do you lay out pest control services?
Group them by pest, not by treatment method. People know what they saw, not what the treatment is called.

solar-website.intro: Going solar is a big decision with lots of steps. These templates include a roof and bill estimator, the install timeline from survey to switch-on, panel and battery options, financing, a service promise and a free assessment form.
tips: Start from the visitor's roof and bill.
Show every step from survey to switch-on.
Explain panels, inverters and batteries in plain words.
Label estimates clearly and avoid promising exact savings.
faq: What should a solar website include?
An estimate tool, how installation works, equipment options, financing, warranties and aftercare, local coverage and a way to book an assessment.
How do solar websites show savings?
Use a clearly labelled estimate based on the visitor's own bill and roof, and say what could change it.

ai-agent-website.intro: AI agents are easier to trust when people can see what they do. These templates show a live-looking run log, the tools an agent can reach, human approval steps, guardrails, use cases and usage-based pricing.
tips: Show a real run, step by step.
Say what the agent can and can't touch.
Show where a person approves or takes over.
Price by what the buyer can understand, such as resolved tasks.
faq: What should an AI agent website include?
What the agent does, a view of it working, the tools it can use, human approval steps, guardrails, pricing and a way to try it.
How do you explain an AI agent on a landing page?
Show one complete task from start to finish rather than describing the technology.

preschool-website.intro: Parents choosing a preschool want to picture their child's day. These templates walk through a day at preschool, rooms by age, how settling in works, fees and sessions, staff, safeguarding, and a tour booking form.
tips: Show a real day, hour by hour.
Explain how settling in works.
Publish sessions, fees and term dates.
Make booking a visit the main action.
faq: What should a preschool website include?
Ages and rooms, a typical day, sessions and fees, staff, safeguarding and policies, meals, term dates and a way to book a visit.
How do you help parents choose a preschool online?
Show a typical day, the people who will look after their child and how settling in works. Then make booking a visit easy.

apartment-website.intro: Renters want floor plans, prices and availability. These templates include a floor plan browser, available homes with move-in dates, amenities, the neighbourhood, a tour scheduler, a resident login and an application path.
tips: Lead with floor plans, prices and availability.
Show real move-in dates.
Make scheduling a tour take seconds.
Give current residents their own login path.
faq: What should an apartment website include?
Floor plans, prices, availability, amenities, the neighbourhood, a tour scheduler, an application path and a resident login.
How do you show availability on an apartment website?
List homes with floor plan, floor, price and move-in date so renters can compare without calling.

pediatrics-website.intro: Parents visit a pediatric site tired and in a hurry. These templates include a sick-today route, a well-child visit schedule by age, a first visit guide, separate waiting areas, a parent portal, general topics and a booking form.
tips: Put the sick-today route first.
Lay out well-child visits by age.
Explain separate waiting areas and same-day slots.
Keep health topics general and clinician reviewed.
faq: What should a pediatric website include?
Same-day sick visits, well-child visits by age, a first visit guide, the clinicians, after-hours routing, a parent portal and booking.
How is a pediatric website different from a general medical site?
The reader is a parent, so it is organised around a child's age and how urgent today's problem feels.

orthodontics-website.intro: Orthodontic care runs over many months, so people want to see the whole road. These templates compare braces and clear aligners, map the treatment timeline, explain the free consult, show payment plans and include teen and adult paths.
tips: Compare braces and clear aligners side by side.
Map treatment from consult to retainers.
Speak separately to parents and adults.
Show how payment plans work.
faq: What should an orthodontics website include?
Treatment options, how a consultation works, the treatment journey, payment plans, the team, and separate information for parents, teens and adults.
How do you present treatment length on an orthodontic site?
Give general ranges and say the orthodontist will confirm a plan at the consultation.

fertility-website.intro: People reach a fertility clinic after a long road. These calm templates lay out a first consultation, the care pathway, treatments in plain words, transparent costs, support for individuals and couples, and a private enquiry form.
tips: Write gently and avoid promises.
Lay out the care pathway step by step.
Publish costs, including what isn't included.
Offer a private way to ask a first question.
faq: What should a fertility clinic website include?
What happens at a first consultation, tests and treatments, a transparent cost guide, the team, emotional support and a private way to enquire.
Can a fertility website publish success rates?
Rules differ by country and figures need careful context. Check your regulator's guidance. These templates do not include any.

hospital-website.intro: A community hospital site answers practical questions first: where to go, when to visit and what each department does. These templates include departments, outpatient clinics, a minor injuries section, visiting times and a site guide.
tips: Say what the minor injuries unit can and cannot treat, and when to call the emergency number.
Put visiting times and how to find the entrance within one click of the home page.
List departments in plain words, not internal names.
Add your real registrations, inspection reports and accreditation yourself, never sample ones.
faq: What should a hospital website include?
Departments and clinics, how to get a referral, visiting times, directions and parking, minor injuries information and emergency guidance.
How should a hospital site show departments?
As a plain list with a short description of each, who it is for and how to get an appointment, so people do not have to know the hospital's own structure.

mental-health-website.intro: A mental health clinic site has to be calm, clear and honest about how care starts. These templates include assessment and therapy services, a named care coordinator, a route for referring doctors, what each appointment involves and crisis signposting on the page.
tips: Show what to do in a crisis at the top of every page, with your local emergency number.
Explain the first appointment step by step, so people know what to expect.
Tell people how you handle waits and how to find out the current one.
Keep the booking form short and do not ask for health details through it.
faq: What should a mental health clinic website include?
Services, how care starts, who is on the team, how referrals work, what each appointment involves, questions about medicines and family involvement, and crisis guidance.
Should a mental health site show crisis information?
Yes. Say clearly that the clinic is not a crisis service and what to do instead, using your local emergency number and crisis lines.

optometry-website.intro: An eye care site helps people book a test and understand what happens next. These templates include eye tests, children's vision, contact lenses, frames, a table of what each appointment involves and a section on sudden changes in vision.
tips: Say how long each kind of appointment takes.
Tell people what to do about sudden loss of vision, flashes or a painful red eye.
Show which tests you offer for children and from what age.
Replace the sample timings with your own, and add your real registrations.
faq: What should an optometry website include?
Eye tests, children's vision, contact lens fitting and aftercare, frames, opening hours, how to book, and when to seek urgent help.
Should an eye care site list prices?
If you can. A short table of tests and fittings answers the question most people have before they book.

pharmacy-website.intro: A community pharmacy site is used for quick jobs: order a repeat, check hours, ask what a service involves. These templates include repeat prescriptions, medicine reviews, vaccinations, minor ailment advice and travel health, with branch details.
tips: Make ordering a repeat prescription the clearest action on the page.
Show opening hours for each branch.
Say when someone should see a doctor instead.
Check what your regulator allows you to say about medicines and services, and add your real registration.
faq: What should a pharmacy website include?
Repeat prescriptions, services and how long they take, opening hours for each branch, how to reach the pharmacist, and when to see a doctor instead.
Can a pharmacy site take repeat orders online?
The templates show the layout only. The form is sample markup, and a real ordering system needs a secure, compliant service behind it.

real-estate-agent-website.intro: A solo agent's site sells the agent as much as the homes. These templates include current listings, a featured home with room sizes, how buying and selling with one agent works, the small team behind the agent, fees and a way to book a call.
tips: Put your current listings and a way to book a call on the first screen.
Show who does what: you, your transaction coordinator, your photographer.
Explain your fee and what it covers in one table.
Add your real licence number yourself, never a sample one.
faq: What should a real estate agent website include?
Current listings, a short bio, how you work with buyers and sellers, your fee, the areas you cover, your licence details and a contact or booking form.
Can a solo agent use the word Realtor on a site?
Only members of the trade association that owns the mark may use it, and the rules for how it is written are strict. These templates say real estate agent.

property-management-website.intro: A property management site has two audiences: owners who want a rental looked after, and tenants who need to pay rent or report a repair. These templates give each their own path, with management plans and fees, available rentals and an emergency repair line.
tips: Give tenants a clear way to report a repair and an emergency line near the top.
Show management plans and fees in one table.
List the rentals you have available now, with monthly rent and move-in date.
Say what owners receive each month, such as a statement and inspection photos.
faq: What should a property management website include?
Services for owners, plans and fees, available rentals, a tenant section for rent and repairs, an emergency line, the team and contact details.
Should tenants and owners share one page?
They can, if each has its own clearly labelled section. Tenants usually need the repair line and payment details; owners need fees and reporting.

luxury-real-estate-website.intro: A luxury agency site is quieter: fewer homes, larger pictures and more about how viewings and discreet sales work. These templates include a featured estate with a floor plan, listings with price on request, private viewing steps and a seller section.
tips: Describe concrete features, such as plot size, views and outbuildings, rather than superlatives.
Explain how private viewings and identity checks work before anyone asks.
Allow price on request where a seller wants it.
Keep a separate, discreet path for sellers.
faq: What should a luxury real estate website include?
A small set of homes with large images, a featured property with room sizes, how private viewings work, the team, the areas covered and a confidential contact form.
How do luxury sites handle homes that are not publicly listed?
Usually with a register-your-interest form and a note that some homes are shown only to qualified buyers.

commercial-real-estate-website.intro: A commercial property site is about space, terms and use. These templates include available offices, shops and industrial units with size, rent per sq ft and use, a featured building with floor areas, lease terms explained, and a section for landlords and investors.
tips: Show rent per sq ft, size and use on every listing.
Explain lease terms such as service charge and break clauses in plain words.
Separate occupier and landlord paths.
Add your real licence and regulatory details yourself.
faq: What should a commercial real estate website include?
Available spaces with size, rent and use, a building or unit feature, services for occupiers and landlords, lease terms explained, the team and offices.
How should commercial listings show price?
As rent per sq ft per year for leases, or a sale price for freeholds, with service charge stated separately.

vacation-rental-website.intro: A direct-booking holiday rental site needs the stays, the dates and the terms. These templates include stays with sleeps, bedrooms and a price per night, a featured stay with its rooms, how booking and check-in work, house rules and a section for owners.
tips: Show sleeps, bedrooms and a from-price on every stay.
Put booking terms, deposit and cancellation in one table.
Tell guests how check-in works before they book.
Describe step-free features exactly instead of making a general accessibility claim.
faq: What should a vacation rental website include?
Stays with photos and key facts, availability or a booking path, booking terms, check-in instructions, house rules, the local area and contact details.
Why book direct on a holiday rental site?
Guests deal with the owner or manager directly. The site should still state the deposit, cancellation terms and how payment is taken.

home-builder-website.intro: A new-home builder site sells plans and places. These templates include home plans and move-in-ready homes across communities, a featured plan with room sizes, how building a new home works, standard and upgrade options, and a path for buyers who have a home to sell.
tips: Show from-prices, beds, baths and size on every plan.
Explain the build stages and when buyers visit the site.
Separate standard specification from upgrades.
Point to the contract for warranty details instead of summarising them.
faq: What should a home builder website include?
Communities, home plans and move-in-ready homes, a plan with room sizes, the build process, standard and upgrade options, sales centre hours and contact details.
Should a builder list prices?
Yes, as from-prices, with a note on what is included and that final prices depend on the plot and options.

bakery-website.intro: A bakery site answers what is baked today, when it comes out of the oven and how to order ahead. These templates include a priced counter menu with a sample dietary key, celebration cake and bread pre-orders with collection times, opening hours, wholesale and classes.
tips: List what is baked each day and roughly when it comes out of the oven.
Give celebration cakes their own order path with the notice you need.
Say plainly which allergens are handled in the bakery, and check every label with the kitchen.
Put collection times and opening hours together.
faq: What should a bakery website include?
Opening hours, a counter menu with prices, how to pre-order cakes and bread, collection times, wholesale information and contact details.
Should a bakery take orders online?
A simple pre-order form with a collection date works for most small bakeries. Say how much notice you need for cakes and how payment is taken.

pizzeria-website.intro: A pizzeria site needs the menu, the ways to get a pizza and the hours. These templates include a priced pizza menu with a sample dietary key, table booking or collection times, a delivery area, lunch slices, party trays and opening hours.
tips: Show dine in, collection and delivery as three clear options.
Put the menu on the page as text with prices.
State the delivery area and the times you deliver.
Keep the phone number in the header for orders.
faq: What should a pizzeria website include?
The menu with prices, how to order for collection or delivery, a delivery area, table booking, opening hours and the address.
Do pizzerias need online ordering?
Many take orders by phone and online. A template can show the menu and a collection-time picker; connect a real ordering system before you take payments.

bar-website.intro: A bar or pub site answers what is on tap, what is on this week and whether you can book. These templates include a drinks and snacks menu with prices, quiz and music nights, table and room booking, a sample house policy on ID and children, and opening hours.
tips: List drinks as text with prices, including alcohol-free choices.
Put the week's events in one place.
Say whether tables and the back room can be booked.
State your house policies plainly and check them against the rules where you trade.
faq: What should a bar website include?
Opening hours, a drinks and food menu, events, table or room booking, house policies and how to find you.
How should a bar website handle alcohol?
Keep the tone responsible: list alcohol-free drinks, avoid promotions of excess, and follow the advertising and licensing rules where you trade.

catering-website.intro: A caterer's site turns interest into a quote. These templates include sample packages with per-guest prices, a quote or tasting request with guest numbers, how planning works, booking terms, the team and office hours.
tips: Show sample packages with a per-guest price range.
Ask for date, guest numbers and service style in the first form.
Explain the steps from enquiry to the event day.
Put deposits and final-numbers deadlines in one table.
faq: What should a catering website include?
Event types, sample menus or packages with prices, a quote request, how planning works, terms, and contact details.
How do caterers price on their website?
Most show a from-price per guest for sample packages and give a full quote after the date, numbers and service style are known.

food-truck-website.intro: A food truck site answers where you are this week. These templates include the weekly route and regular stops, a priced menu with a sample dietary key, pre-order for pickup at a stop, private hire for events and how to pay.
tips: Put this week's stops and times at the top.
Keep the menu short and priced.
Offer pre-order for pickup so queues move faster.
Give private hire its own enquiry path.
faq: What should a food truck website include?
The weekly route or schedule, the menu with prices, pre-ordering, private hire and event bookings, payment options and contact details.
How do food trucks share their location?
A weekly route on the home page, updated when plans change, works well with a note on where to check for same-day changes.

fine-dining-website.intro: A fine dining site sells the booking. These templates include a reservation panel with time slots, the tasting menu course by course with a sample dietary key, drinks pairing, booking and deposit terms, the private room and gift experiences.
tips: Put the booking panel in the first screen.
Show the tasting menu course by course, with the price per guest.
State deposits, cancellation and dietary questions before people book.
Keep the copy quiet and specific.
faq: What should a fine dining website include?
Reservations, the menu or a sample of it, prices, booking and deposit terms, dress code, private dining, gift experiences and how to find you.
Should a tasting menu restaurant show prices?
Yes. Showing the price per guest and any pairing price before booking avoids surprises and missed tables.

tabs.intro: Tabs let people switch between related panels without leaving the page. Each example here is a working tab list with a count badge and a disabled tab, built to the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: arrow keys move between tabs, Home and End jump to the ends, and only the selected tab sits in the tab order. Eight styles, light and dark, with the HTML, CSS and a few lines of plain JavaScript.
tips: Keep tab labels to one or two words so the row does not wrap; let it scroll sideways on phones rather than shrinking the text.
Mark the selected tab with more than colour: an underline, a filled pill or a weight change.
Use tabs for peer views of the same thing. If the content is a sequence, use a stepper; if people need to compare panels, show them side by side.
Give the tab list an aria-label and keep each panel focusable (tabindex="0") so keyboard users can reach content without many Tab presses.
faq: Should tabs switch on arrow keys or on Enter?

Automatic activation (the panel changes as focus moves) is the common choice when panels are already loaded, and it is what these examples do. If a panel is slow to load, switch to manual activation, where arrows move focus and Enter or Space shows the panel.
Can a tab be disabled?
Yes. These examples mark it aria-disabled="true", draw it faded and skip it with the arrow keys. Explain why it is unavailable somewhere nearby, for example in the panel or a tooltip.

cards.intro: Cards group an image, a title and a few facts into one clickable unit. These product cards use one real link per card, stretched over the whole card, so mouse users can click anywhere while screen readers hear one clear link name instead of four. They include a sale price, a badge and a sold-out card, in eight styles with light and dark tokens and plain HTML and CSS.
tips: Use one link per card and stretch it with a ::after overlay; avoid wrapping the whole card in <a>, which makes the link name long and repetitive.
Show focus on the card itself (outline on :has(:focus-visible)) so keyboard users can see the whole target.
Keep the same structure in every card so people can scan prices and titles in a straight line.
Say why a card is unavailable in text (Sold out, Back in January), not only with a faded image.
faq: How do I make a whole card clickable and still accessible?

Put a normal link on the card title and give it a ::after pseudo-element that covers the card (position:absolute; inset:0). The whole card responds to clicks, there is one tab stop, and the link name is just the title.
Do cards need ARIA roles?
No widget role is needed. An <article> or list item with a heading is enough; the heading gives screen reader users a quick way to jump between cards.

pagination.intro: Pagination splits a long list into pages people can step through. These examples show previous and next links, numbered pages, the current page, collapsed gaps and a result range, wrapped in a nav labelled Pagination with aria-current on the current page. On phones they fold down to previous, current and next. Eight styles, light and dark, with HTML, CSS and a small demo script.
tips: Always show where people are (Page 3 of 65 or Showing 41–60 of 1,284) next to the controls.
Make page links at least 40 px square so they are easy to hit on touch screens.
Keep pagination as real links (?page=4) so pages can be shared and crawled; the script here only re-renders the demo.
On page 1, show Previous as disabled rather than removing it, so the row does not jump around.
faq: Pagination or infinite scroll?

Pagination suits lists people come back to, compare or share (search results, catalogues, archives) because each page has an address. Infinite scroll suits feeds people browse once. A Load more button is a middle ground.
How should the current page be marked up?

Put aria-current="page" on the current page's link and give the whole control a nav landmark with aria-label="Pagination". Screen readers then announce the current page and let people jump straight to the control.

popover.intro: A popover is a small non-modal panel anchored to a button, for a short form or extra details. These share popovers open from a button with aria-expanded, move focus into the panel, and close on Escape or a click outside, returning focus to the button. They follow the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern without trapping focus, in eight styles with light and dark tokens.
tips: Keep popovers short: one task, one or two fields. Anything longer belongs in a modal or its own page.
Move focus into the popover when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes, so keyboard users never lose their place.
Close on Escape and on a click outside; do not close while people are still typing.
Leave room at the screen edge on phones: the panel here is never wider than the screen minus 40 px.
faq: What is the difference between a popover and a tooltip?
A tooltip is a short text label that appears on hover or focus and holds nothing interactive. A popover opens on click, can hold buttons and fields, and stays open until it is dismissed.
Should a popover trap focus?
No. A popover is non-modal, so people can Tab out of it; these examples close it when focus leaves. Use a modal dialog with a focus trap only when the rest of the page must wait.

tooltip.intro: Tooltips give icon buttons and unfamiliar terms a short text hint. These examples show the hint on hover and on keyboard focus, keep it open while the pointer is over it, and hide it on Escape without moving focus, as WCAG 1.4.13 asks. The bubble has role="tooltip" and names or describes its trigger. Eight styles, light and dark, HTML and CSS with a few lines of JavaScript.
tips: Never put essential information only in a tooltip; touch screens have no hover.
Keep tooltip text to a short phrase. If it needs a link or a button, use a popover instead.
Use the tooltip as the accessible name of an icon-only button (aria-labelledby) so the label and the hint are the same text.
Keep a disabled button focusable (aria-disabled instead of disabled) when its tooltip explains why it is unavailable.
faq: Do tooltips work on mobile?
Not reliably, because there is no hover. These examples also show on focus, but for touch screens put important hints in visible text and keep tooltips as a desktop extra.
Which ARIA attributes does a tooltip need?
Give the bubble role="tooltip" and an id, then point to it from the trigger with aria-describedby (or aria-labelledby for an icon-only button). The tooltip must not take focus itself.

dropdown-menu.intro: A dropdown menu tucks a list of actions behind one button. These examples follow the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern: Enter, Space or the arrow keys open the menu, arrows move between items, Home and End jump to the ends, typing a letter jumps to a matching item, a disabled item is skipped and Escape closes the menu and returns focus. Eight styles, light and dark, with HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript.
tips: Use a menu for actions (Rename, Duplicate, Delete). For choosing a value in a form, use a native <select> or a listbox instead.
Group items and put destructive actions last, after a separator.
Keep disabled items visible but faded so people learn the option exists, and say why elsewhere.
Close the menu after an action and confirm what happened, for example in a polite live region.
faq: Dropdown menu or select?
A select (or listbox) picks a value that is submitted with a form. A menu runs a command straight away. Screen readers announce them differently, so pick the role that matches what happens.
Why tabindex="-1" on menu items?
Menu items are reached with the arrow keys, not Tab. Setting tabindex="-1" lets the script move focus to them while keeping the whole menu a single tab stop.

accordion.intro: Accordions stack sections that expand in place, so long content stays scannable. In these examples every header is a real button inside a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls, each panel is a labelled region, and arrow keys, Home and End move between headers. One section is open and one is disabled. Eight styles, light and dark, with HTML, CSS and a few lines of JavaScript.
tips: Use a <button> inside a heading for each header, not a div with a click handler.
Show the open state with a rotating chevron or plus sign, not colour alone.
Open the first section by default when it holds the answer most people need.
Avoid accordions for content almost everyone must read; just show it.
faq: Should only one accordion section be open at a time?
Not necessarily. Letting several stay open helps people compare answers; these examples allow it. Closing others automatically can make the page jump.
Can I use <details> and <summary> instead?
Yes, for simple cases. Native details elements need no script, but you cannot add arrow-key movement between headers or use a heading level, which the ARIA pattern here provides.

radio-group.intro: Radio buttons let people choose exactly one option from a short list. These option cards use native radio inputs inside a fieldset with a legend, so the browser handles the keyboard: Tab enters the group at the checked option and the arrow keys move and select. Each option has a hint linked with aria-describedby, and one is disabled. Eight styles, light and dark, HTML and CSS only.
tips: Use radios for two to six visible options; use a select for long lists.
Pre-select the most common or safest option when there is one.
Make the whole card the click target by wrapping the input and text in one <label>.
Restyle the native input with appearance:none rather than hiding it, so focus and forced-colours mode still work.
faq: Radio buttons or a toggle switch?
A switch turns one setting on or off and takes effect straight away. Radios choose one option from several, usually as part of a form that is then saved or submitted.
How do I style radio buttons without breaking accessibility?
Keep the real <input type="radio">, set appearance:none and draw the circle and dot with CSS on the input itself. Labels, keyboard support and screen reader announcements keep working.

breadcrumbs.intro: Breadcrumbs show where a page sits in the site and give a one-click way back up. These examples are a nav labelled Breadcrumb around an ordered list of links, with aria-current on the current page and separators drawn in CSS so screen readers do not read them. A long trail collapses behind a show-more button, and on phones the trail folds to a back link to the parent. Eight styles, light and dark.
tips: Start at the home page and end at the current page, in the same order as the site's structure.
Draw separators with CSS, not as text characters screen readers would read out.
Collapse long middle levels behind a button rather than truncating every label.
On small screens a single back link to the parent is often clearer than a wrapped trail.
faq: Should the current page be a link?
It can be either. These examples keep it as a link with aria-current="page", which the WAI-ARIA breadcrumb example also does; styling makes clear it is where you are.
Do breadcrumbs help SEO?
They give search engines clear internal links and structure, and BreadcrumbList structured data can show the trail in results. The main reason to add them is still navigation for people.

toggle-switch.intro: Toggle switches turn a setting on or off and apply it straight away. Each switch here is a button with role="switch" and aria-checked, named by its visible label and described by a hint, with Space and Enter to flip it and a disabled switch that says why. Eight styles, light and dark, with HTML, CSS and two lines of JavaScript.
tips: Use a switch only when the change applies immediately; inside a form that is saved later, use a checkbox.
Write labels as the setting, not the action (Weekly email digest, not Turn on digest).
Show on and off with position as well as colour, and keep the off track visible against the background.
Put the switch at the end of the row and let the label text sit on the left.
faq: Switch or checkbox?

Both are on/off controls. A switch suggests an instant change, like a light switch; a checkbox suggests a choice that is submitted later. Screen readers announce role="switch" as on or off and a checkbox as checked or not checked.
Should a switch show On and Off text?
Not required if the thumb position and colour change are clear, and the label states the setting. If your switches sit far from their labels, adding small On/Off text helps.

stepper.intro: A stepper shows progress through a short multi-step task such as signing up or opening an account. These examples mark completed, current and upcoming steps in an ordered list with aria-current="step", spell out each state in hidden text, and announce the new step when people press Back or Next. Horizontal on desktop, vertical on phones, in eight styles with light and dark tokens.
tips: Keep steps to three to six, each named for what people do (Verify identity), not a number alone.
Let people go back without losing what they entered.
Show completed steps with a check and the current step with a ring, not colour alone.
Announce the step change in a polite live region so screen reader users know the content changed.
faq: Should stepper steps be clickable?
Only for steps people have already completed, and only if going back is safe. These examples use Back and Next buttons, which keeps the order clear.
How do I mark the current step for screen readers?
Use an ordered list so the position is announced, put aria-current="step" on the current item, and add visually hidden words such as Completed or Not started to the others.

sidebar-nav.intro: A sidebar holds an app's main navigation in a vertical list. These examples include a current page with aria-current, a count badge with screen reader text, a collapsible Reports group built as a disclosure button, a locked item, and a button that collapses the sidebar to icons while keeping the link names. Eight styles, light and dark, with HTML, CSS and a few lines of JavaScript.
tips: Wrap the sidebar in a nav landmark with a label such as Main.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page" and a strong visual cue (filled background or a side bar).
Keep link text for screen readers when collapsing to icons, and show a tooltip or title on hover.
Limit top-level items to about seven; group the rest under expandable sections.
faq: Should a sidebar use role="menu"?
No. Site and app navigation is a list of links in a nav landmark. The menu role is for application-style command menus and changes how screen readers and keyboards behave.
How should the collapse button be labelled?
Give it aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the sidebar, and change its label between Collapse sidebar and Expand sidebar so the action is always clear.

spinner.intro: Loading spinners tell people something is working when you cannot show progress. These examples include three sizes, a button that shows a busy state and an inline status, with the spinner inside role="status" and visually hidden text so the message is read once. Under prefers-reduced-motion the spin slows down and pulses gently. Pure CSS spinners in eight styles, light and dark.
tips: Show a spinner only after a short delay (about 300 ms) so fast actions do not flash.
Say what is loading (Reading 24 sources…) instead of a spinner on its own.
Keep a busy button focusable with aria-disabled and aria-busy, rather than disabled, so focus is not lost.
For waits longer than a few seconds, show progress or a skeleton of the content instead.
faq: How do I make a loading spinner accessible?
Put it in an element with role="status" together with text such as Loading…, visually hidden if needed, and hide the spinning shape itself from screen readers. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Spinner or skeleton screen?
A spinner suits short waits and actions such as saving. A skeleton suits loading a page or list, because it shows the layout that is coming and feels faster.

music-home.intro: Music app home screens show what to play next. These examples include a home screen with recently played, made-for-you playlists with cover art and new releases, and a library view with playlist, album and artist filters, both with a mini now-playing bar.
tips: Lead with what the listener played last; one tap should resume it.
Keep the mini now-playing bar on every screen, above the tab bar.
Give cover art room: it is how people recognise a playlist.
Use filter chips in the library instead of nested menus.
faq: What goes on a music app home screen?
Recently played, personal playlists, new releases and a persistent now-playing bar. Everything else can live in search or the library.

album-page.intro: Album and artist pages turn a name into something to play. These examples show an album page with large cover art, play and shuffle, a numbered track list with durations and credits, and an artist profile with popular tracks, discography and upcoming shows.
tips: Put play and shuffle next to the cover, not below the track list.
Show track numbers and durations in tabular figures so they line up.
Mark the playing track in the list, not only in the player.
On the artist page, popular tracks first, full discography after.
faq: Should an album page show credits?
Yes, near the end of the track list. Listeners look for writers and producers, and it costs little space.

play-queue.intro: Now playing screens with the queue and lyrics. These examples show the current track with a scrubber and transport, a reorderable up-next queue with an autoplay toggle, and full-screen synced lyrics with the current line highlighted.
tips: Show elapsed and remaining time on the scrubber.
Let people reorder the queue by dragging a visible handle.
Highlight the current lyric line and keep it in the middle of the screen.
Keep transport controls in the same place on every now-playing view.
faq: What is an up-next queue?
The list of tracks that will play after the current one. Listeners can reorder, remove or add tracks, and autoplay fills it when it runs out.

story-viewer.intro: Stories screens for social photo apps. These examples show a photo story viewer with segmented progress bars, the author, a reply field and reactions, and a create-story screen with a camera and gallery picker, text and sticker tools and an audience choice.
tips: Use one progress segment per story so people know how many are left.
Tap right to advance, left to go back, hold to pause; show the reply field at the bottom.
Let people pick the audience before they share.
Keep text tools large enough to use with one thumb.
faq: How long should a photo story show?
Most apps use 5 to 7 seconds per photo, with a hold-to-pause gesture so nobody has to rush.

photo-post.intro: Photo post screens for a social feed. These examples show a post detail with a large photo, author, caption, location, likes and save, a comments preview and related posts, plus a threaded comments view with replies and a comment composer.
tips: Let the photo take most of the screen; put actions directly under it.
Show the comment count and the first comments, then a link to all.
Indent replies one level only; deeper threads are hard to follow on a phone.
Keep the comment composer pinned to the bottom.
faq: What should a photo post detail page include?
The photo, author, caption, location, like and save actions, a few comments and a way to see more posts from the same author or place.

post-composer.intro: Create post screens for photo apps. These examples cover editing before posting (crop, a filter strip, adjust sliders and photo order for a carousel) and the details step (caption with mentions and hashtags, location, tagged people, audience, alt text and a share button).
tips: Split editing and details into two steps so each screen stays simple.
Preview the filter on the real photo, not on a sample.
Ask for alt text in the details step, with a short hint.
Show who can see the post before the share button.
faq: Should a create post flow ask for alt text?
Yes. A short, optional field with a hint makes photos accessible to people using screen readers.

barcode-scanner.intro: Barcode scanner screens for product apps. These examples show a camera viewfinder with a scan frame, torch, recent scans and manual entry, and a scan history list with match results and ingredient flags.
tips: Draw a clear scan frame and say what to point the camera at.
Offer manual entry for damaged or missing barcodes.
Give feedback the moment a code is read: a sound, a vibration or a change in the frame.
Keep recent scans one tap away.
faq: What if the barcode is not found?
Say so plainly, keep the scan, and offer to search by name or add the product. Never show an empty result without a next step.

skincare-routine.intro: Skincare routine app screens. These examples show morning and evening routines with ordered steps, product thumbnails, done checks and wait timers, and a products shelf grouped by step with opened dates, use-by dates, layering notes and scan to add.
tips: Order steps the way people apply them and number them.
Show the product for each step, not only the step name.
Use neutral wording for layering notes; this is a routine planner, not medical advice.
Make scanning the fastest way to add a product.
faq: What should a skincare routine app track?
The steps in order, the product used for each, when a product was opened and when it should be used by. Keep advice general and neutral.

image-editor.intro: Image editor UI with a canvas and toolbar. These examples show a tool rail, the photo on a canvas with crop handles, an adjust panel with exposure, contrast and saturation sliders, zoom and undo, plus a layers view with visibility, lock, opacity and blend mode and a properties inspector.
tips: Keep tools on one side and properties on the other.
Show slider values as numbers people can type.
Put undo, redo and zoom where they are always visible.
Name layers by what they contain, with visibility and lock on each row.
faq: What panels does an image editor need?
